content.text:
Yes, literally. `src/harness.rs:395`:

```rust
command.args(["--resume", session]);
```

Suspense passes the previous run's `session_id` to `claude -p`. Claude Code then loads that conversation's full transcript from `~/.claude/projects/-home-hyphyphyph-piton-repl/<session-id>.jsonl` and sends it to the model ahead of your new prompt. It's the same flag you'd use in the terminal.

Where the id comes from: each run's first output line (`system`/`init`) carries the `session_id`, and that line is saved in the task's `.json` record in `.suspense/history`. On opening the project, `Session::latest` scans the history newest-first for the last id and resumes that. So Suspense sends the *id*, and Claude Code supplies the history behind it.

That's why the context was reaching 900k+ tokens earlier: one transcript (`827f0178…jsonl`, 20 MB) accumulating every file those runs had read. "New conversation" in the chat input drops the id, so the next run starts with no `--resume` and a fresh transcript.
